ns2:section.sectionText: This course introduces the principles and applications of functional multiomics, an emerging field that integrates genomics, transcriptomics, proteomics, and metabolomics data to elucidate the complex relationships within biological systems. Students will learn cutting-edge techniques for data integration, analysis, and interpretation, enabling them to uncover functional insights and gain a holistic understanding of biological networks. Through hands-on practical sessions, students will work with real multiomics datasets, collaborate on research projects, and develop skills in bioinformatics tools and data visualization techniques. This section of this course will count toward the 15 advanced credit hours of Advanced MCB Courses in the MCB undergraduate degree program. Prerequisites: MCB 250, MCB 317 Genetics and Genomics. Students are strongly encouraged to familiarize themselves with RStudio and the basics of programming in R prior to taking this class.
